body:
Found 2026-08-09 in adversarial review of the Kobo annotation read design.

Kobo annotation anchors are KoboSpan-relative: `StartContainerPath` is a CSS-ish selector over
`span#kobo\.X\.Y` ids that are INJECTED at kepubify time, with X = paragraph index and Y =
sentence-span index within that paragraph (`notes/KOBO-PROTOCOL-REFERENCE.md` §10.1). Our
`annotation` table stores those locator paths and offsets (`cps/ub.py:931-941`) but stores NO
fingerprint of the KEPUB artifact they were computed against, and no locator-generation id.

Consequence. [INFERRED] If a book's KEPUB is regenerated — re-ingest, a kepubify version change, a
metadata edit that triggers reconversion, a format change (see `notes/3649-...`) — the injected
KoboSpan numbering can shift. Existing stored anchors then point at different text. A server
snapshot built from them can be complete, internally consistent and etag-correct, and still install
anchors that render in the wrong place or not at all. In the write-back direction it could also
cause Nickel to replace freshly-correct local anchors with stale ones.

This is NOT the same as the already-listed "wrong content/chapter identity" failure, which covers
selecting the wrong book or chapter. This is the SAME logical book at a DIFFERENT rendered content
generation.

Scope beyond write-back: the web reader already re-anchors Kobo-origin highlights against the kepub
(`cps/web.py:3365-3380` serves the kepub when the user has annotations precisely so anchors
resolve). So anchor drift can misplace highlights in the EXISTING read-only feature too, not only in
any future device write. That half is worth checking against a real re-ingested book.

Mitigation direction (not implemented): bind a KEPUB artifact fingerprint into both annotation-row
eligibility and any computed etag, and refuse to serve/anchor when the generation cannot be
identified. `context_string` already exists and is the natural re-anchoring fallback when the
fingerprint mismatches — it stores surrounding text for exactly this purpose.

[UNKNOWN] How often regeneration actually shifts ids in practice, and whether kepubify is
deterministic across versions for an unchanged input.
title: KEPUB regeneration shifts KoboSpan ids and strands existing annotation anchors
